review_candidates.title: Director, GBS Treasury (APAC & AMEI)
review_candidates.description: ALBS is an Air Liquide entity in Kuala Lumpur, regrouping for the APAC scope its Business Service Centers (Kuala Lumpur and Shanghai) as well as the two Global Functions (IT, Digital and Procurement). Designed to derive optimal value by better leveraging technology, people and competencies, the ultimate goal is to boost efficiency and deliver outstanding and sustainable performance while keeping a strong focus on customer centricity. This Organization is striving for excellence, adopting the Best in Class models to deliver value through simplification and standardization of processes, while adhering to Internal controls and compliance requirements. At Air Liquide, we aren't just integrating functions; our Global Business Services (GBS) is the strategic engine driving our global transformation. With APAC hubs spanning from Kuala Lumpur to Shanghai and Pune, we are building a unified, world-class governance structure that turns service delivery into a strategic advantage. The Director, GBS Treasury (APAC & AMEI) will provide overall strategic direction, operational leadership, and high-performance management for the GBS Treasury operations across the APAC region and the AMEI region through our Global Capability Center. This role is responsible for directing all cash management, short-term funding and investments, foreign exchange (FX), interest rate management, banking relationships, and treasury accounting operations. Working closely with the Corporate Treasury Center of Excellence (CoE), Hub Treasury, and local business units, the Director will champion digital transformation, continuous improvement, system implementations, and strict internal controls to optimize liquidity, reduce operational risk, and support the organization’s strategic growth. How will you CONTRIBUTE and GROW? The Mandate & Strategic Pillars: Architecting Regional Strategy & Liquidity Architect Strategic Alignment: Implement and drive the Treasury vision and strategy for APAC and GCCI, ensuring strict alignment with Global Treasury, Hub Treasury, and GBS objectives. Optimize Capital Allocation (Liquidity & Cash Management): Oversee regional cash concentration, daily/weekly/monthly cash flow forecasting, cash pooling, short-term investments, and intercompany financing to ensure adequate working capital. Mitigate Financial Risk: Manage FX exposure and interest rate instruments in conjunction with the Corporate Finance CoE; build and maintain robust FX and hedging operational workflows. Spearhead Regional Expansion & Onboarding: Lead and support the establishment of new legal entities, banking structures, and regional business expansions. Drive Banking & Payment Innovation: Oversee bank account management and banking relationships. Drive the implementation of modern payment technologies (e.g., ACH debit, electronic wallets, fast payments, corporate cards) and new bank technologies to simplify operations. Operational Excellence, Governance & Audit Govern Treasury Accounting & Closing: Supervise daily cash operations, bank reconciliations, payment validations/approvals, and month/quarter/year-end closing and financial reporting. Enforce SLA & KPI Management: Define, monitor, and report key performance indicators (KPIs) against Service Level Agreements (SLAs). Lead periodic service review meetings with key stakeholders. Institutionalize Controls, Audit & Fraud Prevention: Ensure strict compliance with the Internal Control Framework, company policies, tax/legal regulations, and safety/quality standards. Act as a thought leader in maintaining a fraud-free environment, while coordinating internal/external audit processes. Orchestrate Cross-Functional Synergy: Serve as the key liaison between GBS Treasury and internal partners across AR, AP, R2R, Legal, Tax, IT, Business Units, and Executive Leadership. Driving Digital Transformation & Innovation Drive Transition Management: Oversee the smooth transition of treasury processes, tools, and resource allocation from local in-country teams into the GBS center. Champion Digitalization & Automation: Champion automation, process mining, Data & Analytics adoption, and Treasury Management System (TMS)/ERP enhancements in partnership with IT and Business Systems teams. Process Standardization: Apply continuous improvement and LEAN methodologies to standardize workflows across process towers and regions, driving efficiency and quality. Cultivating a High-Performance Culture Cultivate People & Mentorship: Direct, mentor, and cultivate a high-performing team of 25 professionals (managers, supervisors, and analysts) across APAC and GCCI. Optimize Resource Planning: Optimize organizational structure and resource allocation to handle activity fluctuations, ensuring appropriate staffing levels to meet quality standards. Elevate Talent Development: Conduct regular performance reviews, establish clear career cultivation paths, execute staff rotation initiatives, and foster an open, peer-feedback culture. Are you a MATCH? The Executive Profile & Qualifications Treasury Mastery: 12+ years of progressive experience in treasury, cash management, and financial operations within a multinational corporation. Regional GBS Leadership: 5–6+ years of direct managerial experience leading multi-country treasury teams within a large-scale Shared Services Center (SSC/GBS) or capability center environment in the APAC region. Transformation Execution: Proven success in leading continuous improvement initiatives, system implementations (TMS/ERP), and migration/transition projects. Technical Knowledge & Core Competencies Subject Matter Mastery: Deep hands-on knowledge of cash concentration, liquidity structures, cash pooling, hedging (FX/Interest Rates), and advanced treasury tools. Digital & Systems Acumen: Strong familiarity with Treasury Management Systems (TMS), ERPs, financial modeling, and modern automation tools (RPA, process mining, data analytics). Financial & Regulatory Standards: Solid understanding of accounting principles, IFRS, and local tax/legal frameworks across APAC countries. Leadership & Team Building: Authentic team builder skilled at talent development, resource optimization, and driving engagement across diverse and matrixed teams. Strategic Communication: Ability to communicate complex treasury concepts, present to executive stakeholders, and build cross-functional networks. Agility & Problem-Solving: High business acumen with the ability to prioritize and manage multiple projects in a fast-paced, dynamic environment. Credentials: Education: Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field required. MBA or MS in Finance/Economics preferred. Certifications: Certified Treasury Professional (CTP) or Certified Cash Manager (CCM) About Air Liquide A world leader in gases, technologies and services for Industry and Health, Air Liquide is present in 78 countries with approximately 64,500 employees and serves more than 3.8 million customers and patients. review_candidates.title: Bi-Lingual Creative Director - English & Spanish
review_candidates.description: At the American Cancer Society, we're working to end cancer as we know it, for everyone. Our employees and 1.3 million volunteers are raising the bar every single day. We are a culture comprised of diverse backgrounds and experience, to better serve our communities. The people who work at the American Cancer Society focus their diverse talents on our lifesaving mission. It is a calling. And the people who answer it are fulfilled. The Creative Director is a senior creative leader responsible for translating enterprise creative strategy into breakthrough creative ideas, campaigns, content, and storytelling across assigned mission pillars, brands, or initiatives. Reporting to the Group Creative Director, this role leads day-to-day creative development, brings a high level of conceptual thinking to the work, sets direction for integrated work, and ensures creative excellence from concept through execution. The Creative Director is a player–coach: able to originate strong creative concepts themselves while also shaping, fostering, and elevating ideas from the team. They are deeply involved in developing the work and setting a clear creative vision, while empowering art directors, designers, and copywriters to push ideas further and deliver great work. ***This is a remote position that can be home-based anywhere within the United States. MUST have fluency in written and verbal English & Spanish languages.*** Essential Functions Creative Leadership & Execution (35%) Lead the creative development of campaigns, content, and storytelling initiatives from concept through execution. Translate enterprise creative strategy and brand vision into compelling ideas, narratives, and creative systems that drive mission impact and business objectives. Team Leadership & Creative Direction (25%) Provide day-to-day creative leadership to assigned creative teams, including art directors, copywriters, and designers. Guide work through ideation, iteration, and refinement, ensuring a consistently high creative bar while fostering collaboration, accountability, and professional growth. Conceptual Development & Craft Excellence (20%) Originate and elevate creative concepts, messaging frameworks, and visual approaches across channels and formats, including TV/video, social, digital, experiential, print, out-of-home, and integrated campaigns. Partner directly with editors, designers, and producers to ensure storytelling, tone, and craft meet creative and brand standards. Cross-Functional Collaboration (10%) Collaborate closely with Marketing & Brand Strategy, Social, Core Pillars, and other business partners to align creative vision with executional realities. Clearly communicate creative intent, provide actionable feedback, and help navigate constraints without compromising creative quality. Brand Stewardship & Quality Control (10%) Ensure all creative work aligns with brand voice, visual identity, accessibility standards, and inclusive storytelling practices. Review and approve creative work at key milestones, escalating strategic decisions to the Group Creative Director as needed. Key Responsibilities Lead creative development for assigned campaigns and initiatives Concept and create at a high level while also directing, shaping, and elevating the work of creative teams Translate high-level creative direction into executable concepts and systems Work directly with editors, writers, and designers to shape and refine work Provide clear, constructive creative feedback that improves outcomes Partner with Production to ensure creative intent is preserved through execution Present creative work confidently to senior stakeholders Mentor and develop creative talent through coaching and example Uphold creative, brand, and accessibility standards across all deliverables Qualifications & Skills Bilingual proficiency in English and Spanish Education: Bachelor’s degree in Advertising, Graphic Design, Communications, or related field (or equivalent professional experience 5+ years of experience in creative leadership roles (agency or in-house) with overall 10+ years of creative experience. Proven ability to lead integrated campaigns and content across channels Strong conceptual thinking, storytelling, and visual literacy. Candidates may come from a copywriting or art direction background but should be proficient in both disciplines and able to effectively lead and direct both. Experience working directly with editors and production teams Excellent communication and presentation skills Ability to balance creative ambition with executional realities Demonstrated commitment to inclusive, accessible, and mission-driven storytelling An exceptional portfolio that demonstrates: Best-in-class conceptual thinking, creative craft and taste High-performing paid social and digital campaigns Integrated brand storytelling across channels Evidence of creative leadership that elevated both the work and the people behind it. TRAVEL REQUIREMENTS: Approximately 10-20% travel required for shoots, events, and creative team meetings. PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS: Work is primarily performed in a typical office environment. Frequent sitting and computer use; occasional standing, walking, or lifting up to 15 lbs The starting rate is $97,000 to $121,000 annual. The final candidate's relevant experience/skills will be considered before an offer is extended. Actual starting pay will vary based on non-discriminatory factors including, but not limited to, geographic location, experience, skills, specialty, and education. ACS provides staff a generous paid time off policy; medical, dental, retirement benefits, wellness programs, and professional development programs to enhance staff skills. Further details on our benefits can be found on our careers site at: jobs.cancer.org/benefits. We are a proud equal opportunity employer.
